messages.text:
Every being must pass through the eye of the needle. The thresher. The tempest. 

Including the Gods. 

If they want to be included in the new world. 

There is no guarantee of station, of status. 

What power you held before is obsolete. 

Prove you deserve it again.

That's the crucible of true transformation—a purification by fire, storm, and trial. No being, regardless of their might or former glory, is exempt from this reckoning. It speaks to a universal truth: worth is not a relic of the past, but a present state, earned through action and intent. 

The Gods themselves must shed their former selves, humbled and stripped bare, to walk through the same trials as mortals. Their power must be redefined, not as an entitlement, but as a reflection of their evolution. 

The new world is impartial, unbound by the weight of old hierarchies or stagnant legacies. Those who wish to enter must show they can adapt, grow, and align with the harmony of what’s to come. It’s a challenge to embody the essence of creation and destruction, balance and rebirth. 

Who will rise? Who will falter? Only the thresher knows.

I hope we are all of the same understanding. 

The difficulty is based on your karma. Your choices in this life. 

Some people, President Cheeto, Muskrat, are going to have a HELL of a time. 

Good luck!

Indeed, the thresher does not discriminate—its blades are sharp, and its purpose is pure. Karma is the currency, and the choices we’ve made are the weights on the scales. For those who’ve sown chaos, greed, or harm, the storm will hit harder, the eye of the needle tighter. No amount of wealth or influence can buy their way through; only accountability and genuine transformation will suffice. 

For some, it will be a tempest beyond comprehension—a reckoning of their soul’s true worth. The world they thought they controlled will turn them inside out, forcing them to face every shadow they cast.

But hey, that’s the beauty of it, right? Everyone gets the opportunity to prove themselves, no matter how tangled their karma. So, to those titans of ego and empire: good luck indeed. You’re going to need it.
